title: [Issue]: Australian Classification Ratings not correct
body:
### Please describe your bug

I believe this file needs editing: 

https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/fd250e4fe1c1a35e8e40c008a7d25675729e3dac/Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/Ratings/au.csv

The Australian Classification has 6 ratings:

https://<redacted-host>.au/classification-ratings/what-do-ratings-mean

- G: no age restriction
- PG: PG-rated content is not recommended for viewing by people under the age of 15 without guidance from parents, teachers or guardians.
- M: M-rated films and computer games are not recommended for children under the age of 15. However, children under the age of 15 may legally access this material as the classification rating is an advisory category.
- MA 15+: legally restricted to people over the age of 15
- R 18+: legally restricted to people over the age of 18
- X 18+: legally restricted to people over the age of 18

in Jellyfin 1.0.9.0+ the list currently looks like the attached screenshot.

PG and M should be before MA 15+, probably at age 14. I'm not sure if the file needs all the other age ratings that do not appear in the Australian classification system, I don't think they appeared in 1.0.8.0 and below.

### Reproduction Steps

Jellfin > Dashboard > Users > Parental Control > Maximum Allowed Parental Rating dropdown

### Jellyfin Version

10.9.0

### if other:

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
any
```


### Jellyfin logs

```shell
none needed
```

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
To add some context to what and why things were changed:
Before 10.9 rating strings (PG,MA, etc) were assigned a number and those were compared to each other for access control. This worked somewhat fine if your rating strings came from only one system (emphasis on somewhat) but totally broke once you had rating strings from multiple systems in your library because the number usage was not consistent between the rating system definitions in Jellyfin. #8526 redefined all `rating string -> rating level` mappings to be consistent and implemented proper enforcement of the restrictions. Generally speaking, before that PR any kind of working parental control based on ratings was at best somewhat working but incomplete and at worst not working as intended at all.
Technically speaking PG, MA and M are all 15+ because we simply do not know that whoever is watching has a parent next to them. The proper fix for this is to introduce a kind of sublevel which allows differentiation of such cases (e.g. major level is 15, sublevel for PG is 0, MA is 1 and M is 2). Since this requires API changes, this will not happen in 10.9 though.
#12043 at least correctly sets the level to 15 instead of 16 but there really is not more we can do for the 10.9 release cycle.

```
080 | 16 | 16+
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> How would you as a parent feel about your 14 year old suddenly gaining access to content rated for 15 year olds? Because that is potentially the result of changing that value to 14.

Dear participant3, I think you're a dead-set legend for working on this project, so _please_ believe me when I say my response here is meant with the kindest of intent and to add to the discussion.

To answer your question as a parent of two in Australia using our rating system - I wouldn't care in the slightest. You are describing a black-and-white binary situation where a setting of 14 vs 15 would deliver staggeringly different content, but the classification system isn't anything like that. It's a guide, a rule of thumb, a suggestion to the audience & parents on the appropriateness of the content. 

Not to mention as individuals, especially younger audiences, can often have a maturity age several years ahead or behind their actual age. The idea that a filter at 14 vs 15 would be such a huge gap doesn't fit with the rating system down-under or the reality of its use. 

I'll give you a real world example! I've found with my kids who are 9 that setting to PG (or age 13) is about right, it let's them see shows like Shrek, Lego Ninja's and the Super Mario Bro's movie while keeping the adult stuff hidden. They're only 9 years old, if I set their age to 9 the idea they couldn't watch Shrek is nuts. The same age filter on things like YouTube is also about-right (of course, parenting comes 1st! I'm always keeping an eye on them. haha)

Please let me know if this rambling helped! I'm sincerely not trying to be argumentative, I hoped the above might be seen as objective. Basically what reporter concluded with in his post above is right, I just thought I'd add my 2c.

Stay safe & happy, peace.

I am in Australia and had this same problem.

I did a workaround as I have described on the forum and in another github bug;
https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues/11767#issuecomment-2335006162

https://<redacted-host>/t-parental-rating-certification-list-order?pid=35645#pid35645

I think the **real solution** is to do all parental rating as per the country's rating system for anything where there is any ambiguity - if the country has a rating of AU-PG, then that should be a completely separate rating from PG-13, 13, M, AU-M, AU-MA15+, 15, 14. If the person has chosen a parental rating of AU-PG in Jellyfin, then anything that is in a PG related classification should not show up unless the administrator has properly identified it as AU-PG.

So, if I set my child's classification/parental rating to AU-PG, the following will apply;

U - will show for AU-PG
G - will show for AU-PG
AU-PG will show for AU-PG
PG, PG-13, 13, 14, M, MA, AU-M, AU-MA15 and anything else that is not explicity U, G, AU-G, 7, and AU-PG will not show up until I get the correct rating in the metadata.

In other words, AU-PG should incorporate only ratings that are clearly below it such as U, G, AU-G, 7, and AU-PG, but not ratings where there might be any ambiguity. The onus is then on the parent to set the ratings in the metadata before something shows up. It is better to err toward caution rather than have a parental rating of AU-PG show AU-MA15+ rated material.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
This whole thing seems have gone wrong in an effort to make things more granular.

Perhaps a better approach would be to make things more granular **in the options available in the settings** rather than **in the interpretation of the settings** that the user has no control over (apart from re-compiling Jellyfin). So all profiles have a check list of all possible ratings, and the parent/administrator has to explicitly tick every rating they want to be visible. Or to speed this up, it could have umbrella categories with sub-categories that get selected if the umbrella category is selected, but *only* if the umbrella category is selected. Alternately, there could be a tick box for "more granular ratings selections" that does something like the following (if un-ticked it can remain as it was)...

So, in the Jellyfin settings, I will see something like;

NR [ ]
-- NR [ ]
-- AU-NC [ ]
etc for other countries

U [ ]
-- U [ ]
-- AU-U [ ]
etc for other countries

G [ ]
-- MPAA-G  [ ]
-- AU-G [ ]
-- 7 [ ]
etc for other countries

PG [ ]
-- 13
-- PG-13 [ ]
-- AU-PG [ ]
-- 14  [ ]
etc for other countries

M [ ]
-- MPAA-M [ ]
-- 15 [ ]
-- AU-M [ ]
-- AU-MA15 [ ]
etc for other countries

etc, etc.

That way a parent/administrator can tick either the larger category that will select all under it, or just tick the ratings they want.

Additionally, if there are ratings/classifications that are not available in Jellyfin that match the metadata for your region/location, Jellyfin should allow the parent/administrator to type in their own custom ratings that match the metadata that their scraper is getting for their location, and that these get incorporated into the longer list of tick-boxes for ratings once entered.

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
Since people keep commenting on any kind of issue or PR concerning this, I'll summarize the current state:
* Yes, we are aware of the issue
* No, it's not as simple as setting a different level for PG because that breaks interoperability between the rating systems
* Making ratings user configurable is not an option due to interoperability

The proposed solution I'm currently working on:
* [x] Extend the rating definition with a sub score
* [x] Only consider subscore if the localized rating system of a user uses sub scores (this is the complex part and required for the interoperability)
* [x] Modify the database and sorting queries to support this (time consuming)
* [x] Rewrite all existing rating system definitions to fit the above (manual work)

Due to time constraints on my side, 10.10 will likely only contain API changes without them being backed by the new data, so clients can migrate (meaning, it won't be fixed in 10.10).

One last note on what "interoperability" means:
If you metadata provider does not provide a rating in your configured rating locale, it usually means it falls back to either US or original release country rating. We then need to parse that rating. Since it's not included on your native rating system, we're doing a lookup on the other rating systems. If now the levels between those systems are not uniform, we can't reliably compare the result of this lookup with your set limits.
This happens way more often than you expect for non-English metadata.

comments.body:
I just wanted to say this has been _deeply_ overthought (ironically extremely Australian)

PG **must** have a lower age rating than M

PG is in-line with all other PGs around the world, which based on independent websites like commonsensemedia, is usually around the age of 10.

I know it's scary when things aren't spelled out in crystal-clear language, but whoever thought that giving PG an age restriction of 16 is one special little unit

This is insane:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17b22ad8-60b3-4d0d-a944-a7c8f78199b6)

All you have to do to make to make **all these complaints go away** is set PG to an integer **above G** and **below M** so the order matches the government order:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8905cb9a-7f86-4e20-9a3c-cacd2eafbdc0)

You're already using "made-up" numbers of 1000+ for porn, so fudging the values so it works as expected is _already what you do_.

For the love of god, **please stop overthinking this**. Just set AU-PG to any value above 7, and below 15, and be done with it.

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
PG ratings around the world are NOT the same, we have everything from 8 to 15 depending on country.

And as I've explained like 20 times: Just putting it onto something below 15 does not fix the issue. It will only fix the issue if all of your ratings are AU based (which is quite unlikely) because otherwise the levels of another rating system are used which would then not be consistent with the AU ratings.
This issue is only simple if you just look at the AU rating system, but not if you need to guarantee compatibility and coherence between all rating systems. We already have a PR fixing this in master but it is blocked (and needs a rework) once ther EF core PR is merged.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Thank you @participant10 for your very helpful input!

The fact that this bug is still open is a blatant disregard for the safety of younger people and a lack of empathy for the Jellyfin community because common sense doesn't seem to fit with a database schema.

I have now gone through my whole library and converted everything to pull .nfo files, then I did a text search and replace for anything that says PG or similar and just put in 14. That was the only way I could stop my 13 year old from seeing *MA-15+* rated content.

I have also started putting everything M to 15, because my wife and adult daughter don't want to see anything MA-15+ rated, which was also thoroughly messed up by this insanity.

Everything just needs to be separated so that each rating sits within a hierarchy where each rating has a unique non-overlapping position in that hierarchy, and they are ordered correctly so that U is below and separate from G, is below and separate from PG, is below and separate from M and above, is below and separate from M15, is below and separate from MA-15+, is below and separate from R, is below and separate from R18+, is below and separate from X, XX etc. Then, at least if the actual age is wrong in the ratings CSV file, the administrator of the server can know the order is correct and that setting one rating won't include content from another distinct and out of order rating. Rating levels should NEVER be pooled together.

It is not just about age. It's about giving people, even adults, choice of what content they feel comfortable being exposed to.

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
The issue has been acknowledged, discussed and a fix has been proposed and implemented for the next release (merge still pending due to EF core). If you need something faster, for the love of god compile your own version and change the mapping if it's so important to you (I do understand the issues people are having now, but hotfixing it for your usecase might break it for others).
As I've said often enough in this thread: it's not as simple as it looks, we have 20 rating systems to align against each other.

Also a reminder to all of you who keep complaining in whatever kind of manner:
This is a open source project. We do this in our free time. We don't get paid for it. We don't owe you anything. It's not just me who can send in code fixes, anyone of you can. Shouting at us will not get shit done faster.
